name: GoogleFindMyToolsWebUi
description: A self-hosted app that logs into your Google account, polls your Find My Device trackers and Android phones, and forwards each new location to your own Traccar or Nextcloud PhoneTrack server - so you keep your location history on your own infrastructure instead of nowhere. One container, a web UI, nothing else to run. CAUTION: this holds long-lived Google account tokens and live device location data. It defaults to plain HTTP with no auth, meant for a trusted LAN - set HTTP_USER/HTTP_PASSWORD and/or HTTPS_ENABLED below before exposing it any further. First-time Google sign-in installs Chrome/Xvfb/noVNC on demand inside the container (needs outbound internet to Debian's mirrors and storage.googleapis.com the first time only), then walks you through the actual login right in the web UI - no separate VNC client needed. GitHub: https://github.com/P6g9YHK6/GoogleFindMyToolsWebUi

paths.name: Data
paths.description: Everything persisted lives flat in here: Google auth tokens, per-device forwarding config, location history, and logs. Back this directory up.

ports.name: WebUI Port
ports.description: Port the web UI (and its API) listens on.

variables.name: HTTP_USER
variables.description: Set together with HTTP_PASSWORD to require this username/password pair (HTTP Basic Auth) for the whole web UI, including the embedded Google login view. Leave both blank to run without auth (trusted LAN only).

variables.name: HTTP_PASSWORD
variables.description: Paired with HTTP_USER above - see its description.

variables.name: SECRETS_ENCRYPTION_KEY
variables.description: Any string. When set, every credential in auth.yaml (OAuth tokens, FCM credentials, vault keys) is encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM instead of stored as plain text. Losing or changing this makes existing encrypted values unreadable - your only recovery is signing in again.

variables.name: HTTPS_ENABLED
variables.description: Set to 1 to serve HTTPS instead of HTTP on the same port, using a self-signed certificate generated automatically on first start and reused after that. See the Security section of the README before turning this on.

variables.name: TZ
variables.description: Timezone for timestamps shown in the UI and logs, e.g. America/Chicago.

variables.name: GFMT_TLS_SAN
variables.description: Comma-separated extra hostnames/IPs to add to the generated self-signed HTTPS cert (it always covers localhost/127.0.0.1/::1) - set this to your LAN hostname or static IP if you reach this box by either.

variables.name: GFMT_TLS_CERT_PATH
variables.description: Bring your own cert instead of the self-signed one - must point at an existing file inside the container (e.g. under /data), or startup fails rather than silently falling back to self-signed. Set alongside GFMT_TLS_KEY_PATH.

variables.name: GFMT_TLS_KEY_PATH
variables.description: Paired with GFMT_TLS_CERT_PATH above - see its description.

variables.name: GFMT_TLS_VALIDITY_DAYS
variables.description: How long a generated self-signed cert is valid for. Defaults to Apple's ATS cap (Safari/iOS/macOS reject longer-lived certs even after you manually trust them) - raise it if you don't care about Safari.

variables.name: DEFAULT_POLL_INTERVAL_S
variables.description: Fallback poll interval (seconds) for a newly added device before you set its own cron schedule.

variables.name: LOCATE_CONCURRENCY
variables.description: Max number of devices being actively located at once.

variables.name: LOCATE_TIMEOUT_S
variables.description: How long (seconds) to wait for a single locate before giving up.

variables.name: QUERY_THROTTLE_MAX
variables.description: Account-wide rate limit against Google's backend: max calls per QUERY_THROTTLE_WINDOW_S. Also editable live from the Config page - no restart needed.

variables.name: QUERY_THROTTLE_WINDOW_S
variables.description: Window (seconds) the QUERY_THROTTLE_MAX limit applies over.

variables.name: QUERY_MIN_SPREAD_S
variables.description: Minimum spacing (seconds) enforced between individual calls to Google's backend.
